quotes.text: Here's the test you can run right now before you roll out labels, answer in one sentence, what specific business risk will these labels reduce.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A simple, actionable test for label strategy.

quotes.text: If it takes more than three clicks, or if users have to dig through a sub menu to label a file, your taxonomy is too complex.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete rule of thumb against over-engineering.

quotes.text: The biggest stumbling block for most Microsoft Information Protection rollouts isn't technology at all. It's people.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core thesis that adoption, not tech, decides success.

quotes.text: Think of a pilot less as testing the engine and more as testing the driver. The goal isn't to prove the technology works, it's to prove employees can use it without friction.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes what a pilot should measure.

quotes.text: For lasting success, labeling has to feel less like punishment and more like protection. Seeing the why matters as much as configuring the how.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable summary of the human side of labeling.

takeaways: Every label must map to a clearly stated business risk, starting with a small core set such as internal only, personal data, confidential and public.
Over-engineered label hierarchies and poorly prepared users create workarounds, so simplicity and clear communication drive adoption.
Pilot with real business users under real deadlines and reinforce training through microlearning, contextual nudges and manager follow-up.
hook: Many Microsoft Information Protection rollouts look secure on paper while users mislabel files or work around the controls. This episode gives security and compliance teams five quick checks covering purpose, simplicity, resistance, pilots and training. Use them to find out whether your MIP rollout will fail or fly before it goes live.
